title: 1. The edge in light mode
rec_short: Keep it as ruled: invisible in light, grey in dark
q: In light mode the edge token is transparent in all four themes, so a menu has no line at all, only its shadow. You said "it needs an edge". Is the shadow enough in light?
rec: Recommended: Keep it as ruled: invisible in light, grey in dark. The page you answered at 17:49 described this edge as "invisible in light, a grey line in dark", and you said yes to it. A visible light line would be a new value for the token in all four themes.
chips: Keep it as ruled: invisible in light, grey in dark
Give light a visible hairline too

title: 2. The account menu's old grey line
rec_short: The same edge as every other floating surface
q: Before last night the account menu had a light grey line all round, in light mode too. It now uses the floating edge, so in light it has no line. Keep it with the others, or give it back its grey line?
rec: Recommended: The same edge as every other floating surface. One rule for every floating surface, and the mega menu is the only exception you named.
chips: The same edge as every other floating surface
Give it back its grey line

title: 3. The banking dashboard's account menu draws plain browser buttons
rec_short: Fix it at the source
q: Found while rendering: on the banking dashboard, the account menu's items ("Switch to dark theme", "Secure session") draw as unstyled browser buttons, in every theme and both modes. The bottom row of both sheets shows it. Fix it at the source?
rec: Recommended: Fix it at the source. It is a defect, not a design choice. The menu should draw its items the way the top nav's account menu does.

title: 4. Are the four offered for the input role
rec_short: Yes, each of the four is offered for input
q: Should switch, checkbox, radio and chip each be offered as a way for a person to give a value (the input role), beside selection controls? Today only the family is, so a client library looking up "switch" finds it with no role.
rec: Recommended: Yes, each of the four is offered for input. A client library asks for the switch by name. It should find what the switch is for there, not one level up.
chips: Yes, each of the four is offered for input

title: 5. Do the parts that borrow a control name it
rec_short: Yes, point at the control by name
q: The data grid's row checkbox, the transfer list, rating and settings all borrow a control. Should each one point at the checkbox, radio or chip by name, instead of at selection controls?
rec: Recommended: Yes, point at the control by name. It is the same reason as the split itself: what the part uses becomes something a library can look up.
chips: Yes, point at the control by name
No, keep pointing at the family

title: 6. What the family keeps
rec_short: Keep only what the four share
q: Should the family keep its own copy of the control settings (which control, which checkbox kind, which chip kind), or keep only what the four share?
rec: Recommended: Keep only what the four share. Two copies of one setting drift apart. Each member now carries its own.
chips: Keep only what the four share
Keep its own copy as well

title: 7. What "a valid element" means for a template
rec_short: Yes: a template is a page made only of parts
q: The lane read your phrase as: a template is a page, and a page is made only of parts. It places them, never sizes or restyles them, and carries a meta like any other component. The other reading was to keep each template a self-contained component that copies the rules it needs. Is the first reading yours?
rec: Recommended: Yes: a template is a page made only of parts. Your own words say it three times: "the page never sizes a part", "rebuild the shared stylesheet rather than carrying the rules on the page", and the twelve are "whole composed pages". Under the other reading a template could only ever be a copy.
chips: Yes: a template is a page made only of parts
No: a template stays a self-contained component

title: 19. The error page's column
rec_short: The empty-state part
q: The error page now uses the empty-state part (a quiet dashed box, smaller heading, faint glyph) with two buttons under it. The old page was half that and half the confirmation part (no box, a bigger title, a success roundel). Which is the error page's column?
rec: Recommended: The empty-state part. The confirmation part only knows success, and its roundel would be wrong on an error.

title: 20. Do sections on ordinary pages get a surface
rec_short: Sections sit on rules; the settings wording is amended
q: The old templates put page sections on a borrowed card. Since your container rulings, a card is one of a set of like records, and sections are landmarks. The rebuilt pages draw sections on a rule above each. The settings rule still says "sections are grouped on card surfaces". Which wins?
rec: Recommended: Sections sit on rules; the settings wording is amended. It follows your later word, and a page of one-off cards is what the lone-card rule warns about.
chips: Sections sit on rules; the settings wording is amended
Sections get a surface of their own

title: 21. Does every template carry the app frame
rec_short: Yes, every page template carries the frame
q: The bento dashboard carries the top nav and the footer. The plain dashboard and the report now end with the footer but have no nav. The other nine show the page body only. Should every page template carry the app frame?
rec: Recommended: Yes, every page template carries the frame. You called them whole composed pages, and the standing rule is that every app page ends with the app footer.

title: 22. The list index: one form or both
rec_short: Both stay, each chosen by its job
q: The list index still draws both forms: the data grid for bulk approval, and the plain list as the default. For a payments index, is one of them the template, or do both stay as the drawn choice?
rec: Recommended: Both stay, each chosen by its job. Your list rule already decides between them: the grid when rows are selected in bulk, the list otherwise.

rec_short: 40 stands

rec: Recommended: 40 stands. Only ruled masters are drawn, and a new size is a new drawing for you to rule by eye.

title: 24. A password reveal
rec_short: Yes, the library gains a reveal in the field
q: No part draws a password reveal inside the field, and the icon library has no eye. The sign-in page shows a quiet "Show password" button under the box instead. Should the library gain a reveal: an eye in the text field's end slot?
rec: Recommended: Yes, the library gains a reveal in the field. It is the expected pattern on a banking sign-in, and a reveal under the box costs a line of space on every password field.
